title: Part 2 Practice: Temperature and Rainfall Distribution

questions.text: The DEGA climate zone is found at which elevation?
questions.explanation: DEGA (cool highland) is at 2,300-3,200m with temperatures 10-15°C. WEYNA DEGA is 1,500-2,300m (15-20°C). KOLLA is 500-1,500m (20-30°C). BEREHA is below 500m (>30°C).
BEREHA (hot desert, below 500m) has temperatures ABOVE 30°C. Examples include Dallol and Afar lowlands — among the hottest places on Earth.

questions.text: Examine the climate zones diagram. Which is WEYNA DEGA?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='200' viewBox='0 0 350 200'><rect width='350' height='200' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><rect x='40' y='20' width='270' height='30' fill='#f43f5e'/><text x='175' y='40' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Zone A (Above 3200m)</text><rect x='40' y='55' width='270' height='30' fill='#facc15'/><text x='175' y='75' text-anchor='middle' fill='#0B0F19' font-size='9'>Zone B (2300-3200m)</text><rect x='40' y='90' width='270' height='30' fill='#14b8a6'/><text x='175' y='110' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Zone C (1500-2300m)</text><rect x='40' y='125' width='270' height='30' fill='#38bdf8'/><text x='175' y='145' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='9'>Zone D (500-1500m)</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Zone C (green, 1,500-2,300m) is WEYNA DEGA — the warm highland zone where Addis Ababa is located. Zone A is Wurch, Zone B is Dega, Zone D is Kolla.

questions.text: The KIREMT season (main rains) occurs during:
questions.explanation: KIREMT (main rainy season) occurs June to August, caused by the SOUTHWEST MONSOON. This is the critical season for agriculture, with heaviest rainfall in July and August.

questions.text: The BEGA season is characterized by:
questions.explanation: BEGA (December-February) is the DRY season with COOL temperatures, especially in the highlands. There is little to no rainfall during this period. Frost may occur in high altitude areas.

questions.text: The BELG season (short rains) occurs during:
questions.explanation: BELG (short rains) occurs March to May, especially important in SOUTHERN and SOUTHEASTERN Ethiopia. It's a SECONDARY rainy season, less reliable than Kiremt, and critical for pastoralists.

questions.text: Which region receives the HIGHEST annual rainfall in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The SOUTHWESTERN HIGHLANDS receive the HIGHEST rainfall (above 2,000mm annually) due to their position facing the southwest monsoon. This is why they're ideal for coffee growing. Afar and Somali are the driest.

questions.text: Which areas receive the LOWEST rainfall in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The AFAR and SOMALI lowlands receive the LOWEST rainfall (below 500mm annually). These are hot, arid regions with desert-like conditions. The Afar region is one of the hottest and driest places on Earth.

questions.text: The WURCH zone is characterized by:
questions.explanation: WURCH (alpine, above 3,200m) is the COLDEST zone with temperatures below 10°C. Frost is possible, especially at night. Found in Simien Mountains and Bale Mountains. This zone has Afroalpine vegetation.

questions.text: Examine the rainfall seasons diagram. When is the PEAK rainfall?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='160' viewBox='0 0 350 160'><rect width='350' height='160' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><line x1='30' y1='140' x2='330' y2='140' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M 40 130 Q 80 110 110 30 Q 140 20 160 30 L 180 40 L 200 130 L 220 130 L 240 130 Q 270 90 290 60 Q 310 50 320 80' fill='none' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='3'/><text x='100' y='50' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f59e0b' font-size='9' font-weight='bold'>July-Aug</text><text x='290' y='70' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f43f5e' font-size='8'>March-May</text></svg>
questions.explanation: The PEAK rainfall (blue curve highest point) occurs in JULY-AUGUST during the KIREMT season. The secondary peak in March-May is BELG. The lowest point in December-February is BEGA.
